ChIJtX8DBviP4TgRi-vmX3413aU.author: The Unscripted Guide
ChIJtX8DBviP4TgRi-vmX3413aU.text:
I recently visited Cafe Tibet and overall had a really pleasant experience. Starting with the food, the momos were just above average—not bad at all, but not something I would specifically go back for. However, the Chicken Thai Pai completely made up for it. It was absolutely excellent, full of flavor, well-cooked, and easily the highlight of the meal.

Apart from that, the rest of their menu is also very good. There’s a nice variety of dishes, and everything we tried was well-prepared and satisfying. You can tell they maintain a consistent quality across their offerings, which is always a big plus.

One thing that stands out, though, is the pricing. It does feel a bit on the higher side, especially considering portion sizes. That said, the overall experience balances it out to a large extent.

The service was smooth and attentive without being intrusive, which added to the comfort. The atmosphere is amazing—calm, cozy, and thoughtfully designed. What really makes this place special is its unique location, which gives it a distinct charm you don’t find everywhere.

Overall, it’s definitely worth visiting for the ambiance, service, and standout dishes.

ChIJtX8DBviP4TgRi-vmX3413aU.text: I stopped by Cafe Tibet and ordered the chicken fried rice, but it just didn’t deliver that good. The dish arrived only warm when it should have been steaming hot, and the flavor was flat—more oily than savory, with hardly any seasoning to make it stand out. The service was outstanding,the staff member  was quick, friendly, and genuinely attentive, checking in without hovering. Their hospitality is the kind that makes you feel welcome the moment you walk in. I’d happily return for the atmosphere and service, but I’d skip the chicken fried rice and try something else on the menu next time.

ChIJi5-ncgCF4TgR-ChabhQKloM.author: Owais Amin
ChIJi5-ncgCF4TgR-ChabhQKloM.text:
If you're around the University of Kashmir and craving authentic Tibetan food, Café La Hasa is a hidden gem you shouldn't miss! Located right opposite Sir Syed Gate, this spot serves the tastiest momos and chowmein in town. The momos are perfectly steamed with juicy fillings, and the chowmein is packed with flavor and just the right amount of spice.

But it’s not just the food that stands out—the café’s interiors give off a completely different vibe from other places in the area. Decorated in a traditional Chinese style, the space feels unique and cozy, offering a refreshing change from the usual café setups. The calm and peaceful atmosphere makes it an ideal spot to unwind, far from the usual noise and buzz of the city.

The staff is incredibly friendly and polite, always making you feel at home. Their service is quick, and they’re more than happy to recommend something if you’re unsure what to try.

Whether you're looking for delicious Tibetan food, a serene environment, or a unique ambiance, Café La Hasa checks all the boxes. Definitely worth a visit!
